documents.title: Guideline: Responsible Use of Generative AI in Academic Work
documents.stance_why: The guideline says instructors have "complete autonomy" and must put a policy statement in the syllabus, offering three sample statements (Open, Restricted, Prohibited Use); it sets no single rule itself, so it delegates and lists the tiers.
documents.summary: Provost guideline that tells students to follow each course's GenAI rule, disclose use, protect data, and ask when unsure. It requires instructors to put a syllabus statement and supplies three sample statements, disclosure templates and a list of licensed tools.

units.why: The Context paragraph frames the guideline: the university "supports the exploration and responsible use" of GenAI, so it is a framework statement of purpose (P56) rather than a rule for a single course; it is institution-level and general.
units.anchor: supports the exploration and responsible use GenAI technologies to enhance student learning
units.frag_start: The Florida Institute of Technology recognizes
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance permit, B neutral. The sentence 'supports the exploration and responsible use GenAI technologies to enhance student learning' welcomes responsible use, so it takes a position on AI use; permit (not encourage) because the same sentence conditions it on responsible use.

units.why: "must align with the university's commitment to academic integrity, ethical standards" sets the principle every GenAI use is bound by; I chose P56 (framework principle) over P36 because it names no sanction.
units.anchor: must align with the university’s commitment to academic integrity, ethical standards

units.why: "must adhere to specific policies and guidelines set by the course instructor" places the rule-setting with each instructor, so students follow the course policy; this is P04 (per-instructor rule).
units.anchor: Students must adhere to specific policies and guidelines set by the course instructor
units.resolution_why: A during-work, B course-start. The rule binds students as they do coursework ('must adhere to specific policies ... set by the course instructor'); communication of expectations is covered by the instructor-side syllabus units, so during-work.

units.why: "must consult the course instructor if they are uncertain" tells unsure students to ask before using AI, which is exactly P10.
units.anchor: Students must consult the course instructor if they are uncertain
units.resolution_why: A during-work, B before-course. The duty to consult applies 'before utilizing them for coursework', i.e. at the point of doing work, and is not course or policy design, so during-work.

units.why: "without instructor approval is considered a violation of academic integrity" makes unapproved AI use a violation, so absent permission AI is not allowed. I chose P06 (fallback when no permission is given) as the main type; it is also misconduct (P36) but the rule defines the default.
units.anchor: without instructor approval is considered a violation of academic integrity
units.frag_start: The use of GenAI tools in coursework
units.frag_end: without instructor approval is considered a violation of academic integrity.

units.why: "must clearly disclose the use of GenAI tool(s) and their specific contribution ... by providing proper citations" requires disclosure and citation with each submission where AI is allowed (P24).
units.anchor: students must clearly disclose the use of GenAI tool(s) and their specific contribution
units.frag_start: In instances where GenAI use is allowed,
units.resolution_why: A unit_stance require, B permit. The passage starts 'In instances where GenAI use is allowed', so disclosure is a condition on permitted use. Nothing requires AI use, so permit, not require.

units.why: "Students are fully responsible for ... the appropriateness, accuracy and originality of their work" makes students own what they submit (P29).
units.anchor: Students are fully responsible for the ethical use of GenAI

units.why: "must consider the ethical implications ... including potential biases, misinformation" asks students to weigh bias, privacy and IP concerns, which is P53; the data-privacy part is coded separately as P50.
units.anchor: must consider the ethical implications of using GenAI tools in their coursework

units.why: "must avoid inputting sensitive information ... into external AI platforms" protects confidential data, P50 (not P20, which is about assignment specs and code).
units.anchor: Students must avoid inputting sensitive information
units.resolution_why: A must-not, B must. The source says students 'must avoid inputting sensitive information', which is a prohibition on inputting it, so must-not.

units.why: "students should discuss with their instructors if they have any concerns about equitable access" addresses access to required AI tools (P51).
units.anchor: students should discuss with their instructors if they have any concerns about equitable access
units.frag_start: In instances where an AI tool

units.why: "Students are encouraged to explore the use of AI tools to support their ability to think critically" welcomes AI use by default (P02).
units.anchor: Students are encouraged to explore the use of AI tools
units.resolution_why: A during-work, B general. The sentence encourages students to explore AI tools to support critical thinking and problem solving, which is about doing and studying work, not definitions or scope, so during-work.

units.why: "to complement or enhance their skills rather than replace their own critical thinking" keeps students as the primary thinker (P32).
units.anchor: rather than replace their own critical thinking or intellectual growth
units.resolution_why: A neutral, B encourage. The sentence says students 'are encouraged to leverage AI technologies to complement or enhance their skills', which welcomes use within a limit, so encourage.

units.why: "Students should strive to understand the basis and limitations of AI-generated content rather than simply accepting it" asks students to evaluate output critically (P31).
units.anchor: understand the basis and limitations of AI-generated content

units.why: "complete autonomy in determining the pedagogical use of GenAI tools" delegates the decision to instructors (P04).
units.anchor: a course instructor has complete autonomy in determining the pedagogical use of GenAI tools
units.frag_start: The Florida Institute of Technology acknowledges

units.why: "in strict compliance with the principles of Florida Tech policy on Student Academic Honesty" bounds instructor discretion by the honesty policy; I chose P56 as a framework limit, not P36, because no sanction is stated.
units.anchor: exercised in strict compliance with the principles of Florida Tech policy on
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. Source: 'This discretion is exercised in strict compliance with the principles of Florida Tech policy on Student Academic Honesty.' It limits instructor autonomy, so it is a real policy statement. Kept; B folded instructor autonomy into one unit.

units.why: An instructor who requires GenAI "must ensure students have equitable access ... or the assignments can be completed using a free version", so required tools may not create a paywall (P51).
units.anchor: must ensure students have equitable access to the respective tool
units.frag_end: free version of the GenAI tool adopted for the course.

units.why: "Instructors are required to incorporate a course policy statement into their course syllabi" is a syllabus-statement mandate (P09).
units.anchor: Instructors are required to incorporate a course policy statement into their course syllabi
units.frag_end: approach to GenAI use in their courses.
units.resolution_why: A before-course, B course-start. 'Instructors are required to incorporate a course policy statement into their course syllabi' is about putting the expectation in the syllabus for students, as in the neighbouring syllabus unit, so course-start.

units.why: "The course syllabus must clearly state whether the use of GenAI tools in coursework is allowed (restricted or unrestricted use) or not (prohibited use)" restates the syllabus mandate and sorts uses into three kinds; P09 fits best, the tiers themselves are coded under P05.
units.anchor: The course syllabus must clearly state whether the use of GenAI tools in coursework
units.frag_start: The course syllabus must clearly state

units.why: The guideline offers three sample syllabus statements named "Open Use", "Restricted Use" and "Prohibited Use", which are named tiers of AI use (P05); instructors choose among them, hence document stance delegates.
units.anchor: Option 1: Open Use
units.policy: The guideline offers three sample syllabus statements for instructors to adapt: Option 1 Open Use, Option 2 Restricted Use, Option 3 Prohibited Use.
units.resolution_why: A before-course, B course-start; both P05 and neutral. The three options are samples that instructors choose from and adapt when designing the course policy, so before-course.

units.why: Option 1 says the course "encourages the exploratory use of generative AI tools" and permits brainstorming, research assistance and writing support: a permissive default (P02) for courses that adopt it.
units.anchor: encourages the exploratory use of generative AI tools as part of the learning process
units.frag_end: as part of the learning process.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. Source: Option 1 sample says 'This course encourages the exploratory use of generative AI tools as part of the learning process.' It is a separate sentence with its own stance (encourage), so kept.

units.why: Option 1 lists the allowed purposes "brainstorming, research assistance, and writing support"; I coded brainstorming (P15) as the type since the list is led by it, and the prose uses are covered by the sentence under P02.
units.anchor: permitted to use generative AI (GenAI) technologies for brainstorming, research assistance, and writing support
units.resolution_why: Codes agree. Anchor widened to B's fuller span so that it names all three permitted uses (brainstorming, research assistance, writing support).

units.why: Option 1: "all use of GenAI must be clearly disclosed, and students are responsible for the final content" requires disclosure under open use (P24).
units.anchor: all use of GenAI must be clearly disclosed
units.frag_start: However, all use of GenAI must
units.resolution_why: A unit_stance require, B permit. This is the disclosure condition inside the Open Use sample, where use is permitted; AI use is not required, so permit.

units.why: Option 1: GenAI "not replace original thought or fundamental skills such as critical thinking, problem-solving, and writing" protects fundamentals and student thinking (P32).
units.anchor: not replace original thought or fundamental skills such as critical thinking,
units.frag_start: GenAI should be used to enhance
units.resolution_why: A neutral, B permit. The sentence limits use ('not replace original thought or fundamental skills') and takes no position on whether to use AI itself, so neutral, as for the same rule elsewhere.

units.why: Open Use sample: "specific instructions for particular assignments will be communicated" lets assignments override the course rule (P04).
units.anchor: specific instructions for particular assignments will be communicated to students as necessary
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. Source (Option 1 sample): 'Any exceptions to the syllabus guidelines for GenAI use or specific instructions for particular assignments will be communicated to students as necessary.' It states that the instructor will communicate assignment-level rules, a real statement. Kept.

units.why: Option 1: "not permitted to use GenAI ... in a way that would violate the Academic Honesty Policy" ties open use to misconduct rules (P36).
units.anchor: not permitted to use GenAI in their academic work in a way that would violate
units.frag_start: Students are not permitted to use
units.resolution_why: A when-misuse, B during-work. The sentence tells students how they may use GenAI in their academic work ('not permitted ... in a way that would violate the Academic Honesty Policy'); sanctions are handled in the separate 'will be considered a violation' units, so during-work.

units.why: Option 2 permits GenAI "under specific conditions" for listed purposes such as outlining or proofreading, a narrow-permission tier (P05).
units.anchor: is permitted in this course under specific conditions

units.why: Option 2 sets a blank for prohibited uses ("writing full essays, solving problem sets, code generation"): students may not have AI produce submitted work (P19).
units.anchor: the use of generative AI tools is NOT allowed for

units.why: Option 2: "All GenAI use must be explicitly disclosed in submitted work" (P24).
units.anchor: All GenAI use must be explicitly disclosed in submitted work
units.resolution_why: A unit_stance require, B restrict. Disclosure is a condition on the uses that the Restricted Use sample permits; AI use is not required and the sentence does not limit the uses, so permit.

units.why: Option 2: failing to follow the guidelines "will be considered a violation of academic integrity", which classifies misuse as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: will be considered a violation of academic integrity
units.frag_start: Failure to follow these guidelines or
units.resolution_why: A must-not, B informs. 'Failure to follow these guidelines ... will be considered a violation of academic integrity' classifies breaches as misconduct; the prohibition itself is in the preceding 'NOT allowed' unit, so informs.

units.why: Restricted Use sample: tools "should be used to enhance understanding and creativity, not replace original thought" (P32).
units.anchor: should be used to enhance understanding and creativity, not replace original thought or fundamental skills
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. Source (Option 2 sample): 'The listed GenAI tool(s) should be used to enhance understanding and creativity, not replace original thought or fundamental skills'. It is a separate passage from the Option 1 version, so kept; unit_stance neutral to match the Option 1 unit.

units.why: Option 3: "the use of generative AI tools is NOT permitted for any assignments in this course" is a blanket ban (P01).
units.anchor: the use of generative AI tools is NOT permitted for any assignments in this course
units.frag_start: the use of generative AI tools

units.why: Option 3: "All work must be completed independently by the student" requires submitted work to be the student's own; P29 fits the ownership rule while P01 is the ban sentence.
units.anchor: All work must be completed independently by the student
units.frag_start: All work must be completed independently

units.why: Option 3: "failure to meet this requirement will be considered a violation of academic integrity" classifies breach as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: failure to meet this requirement will be considered a violation
units.frag_start: and failure to meet this requirement
units.resolution_why: A must-not, B informs. 'failure to meet this requirement will be considered a violation' classifies breaches; the prohibition is in the preceding units (NOT permitted; work completed independently), so informs.

units.why: Option 3 gives a rationale slot: "To ensure the development of critical skills and maintain academic integrity", saying bans protect skill development (P41).
units.anchor: To ensure the development of critical skills and maintain academic integrity
units.resolution_why: A before-course/neutral, B course-start/prohibit. This is the rationale clause ('To ensure the development of critical skills and maintain academic integrity') inside the statement that goes to students; it explains rather than bans, so course-start and neutral. The ban is coded in the next units.

units.why: The three options each end with "please consult your instructor for clarification", an invitation to ask when unsure (P10).
units.anchor: Should you have any questions, doubts, or concerns about using GenAI tools in your coursework,
units.frag_start: Should you have any questions, doubts,
units.resolution_why: A course-start, B during-work. The sentence tells students to ask the instructor when they have questions about using GenAI in coursework, which arises while doing the work, so during-work.

units.why: The guideline supplies disclosure statements "for instructors to adapt/use" so students know how to indicate GenAI use; this is a disclosure mechanism (P24).
units.anchor: statements are for instructors to adapt/use to provide students with guidelines on how
units.policy: Florida Tech provides the disclosure statements for instructors to adapt or use so that students can indicate their use of GenAI in coursework.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. Source: 'The following statements are for instructors to adapt/use to provide students with guidelines on how to indicate their use of GenAI in coursework.' It tells instructors that the disclosure templates may be adapted, so kept, with modality changed from should to may.

units.why: The template asks for "specific generative AI tool(s), version #, access date" and the task, which are tool/version/date details of a citation (P25).
units.anchor: [type name of the specific generative AI tool(s), version #, access date]
units.resolution_why: A neutral, B permit. The tool, version and access date are filled into a disclosure statement for use that is allowed, so permit.

units.why: The general template has students attest they "reviewed, validated, and edited all AI-generated content", a verification duty (P31) built into the disclosure.
units.anchor: reviewed, validated, and edited all AI-generated content included in the submitted work
units.resolution_why: A neutral, B permit. The student statement that AI content was reviewed, validated and edited accompanies allowed use, so permit.

units.why: The Code Generation Support disclosure statement says 'I (or my team) used [tool] to generate the basic framework of this code' and that the code was reviewed, modified, debugged and optimized, so it shows that AI-generated code is allowed when disclosed. It is P16 and may.
units.anchor: to generate the basic framework of this code
units.resolution_why: A informs/P24, B may/P16. The statement is the model wording for code that AI generated and the student reviewed, which is allowing AI-generated code under stated conditions (P16). Disclosure is in the topics, not the type.

units.why: The Writing Support template covers grammar and vocabulary help with "final edits, content, arguments, and final wording" the student's own, a prose-specific disclosure (P18).
units.anchor: for grammatical corrections, sentence structure, and vocabulary suggestions
units.resolution_why: A informs, B may. The sample statement shows AI help with grammar, sentence structure and vocabulary is allowed when disclosed, so may.

units.why: The Problem-solving template shows AI used "to enhance my (our) understanding of" a concept while the student applies the method independently: AI as a tutor (P12).
units.anchor: to enhance my (our) understanding of
units.resolution_why: A informs, B may. The sample statement shows AI used to enhance understanding of a concept is allowed when disclosed, so may.

units.why: The Brainstorming template discloses AI used "to generate initial ideas" with final work independently the student's (P15).
units.anchor: to generate initial ideas for this assignment
units.resolution_why: A informs, B may. The sample statement shows AI used for initial ideas is allowed when disclosed, so may.

units.why: The Citation Assistance template shows AI used "to format and/or organize references", a prose/reference-formatting use (P18).
units.anchor: to format and/or organize references in this assignment
units.resolution_why: A informs, B may. The sample statement shows AI used to format or organize references is allowed when disclosed, so may.

units.why: The Resource Assistance template shows AI used to "identify relevant resources" with information "independently verified" by the student (P31).
units.anchor: All information has been independently verified by me (or my team) for accuracy and appropriateness.
units.resolution_why: A informs, B may. The Resource Assistance statement shows AI used to identify resources is allowed if the student independently verifies the information, so may (type P31 for the verification duty).

units.why: The university lists licensed tools (Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini) students log into with Florida Tech accounts: sanctioned tools (P17).
units.anchor: Florida Tech Licensed Generative AI Tools
units.frag_start: Florida Tech Licensed Generative AI Tools
units.policy: Florida Tech provides licensed generative AI tools: Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini, accessed with Florida Tech accounts.
units.resolution_why: A permit, B neutral. The section lists the licensed tools (Copilot, Gemini) and how to access them; it provides tools but sets no position on use, so neutral.

units.why: "Access is limited to the web browser only. Mobile app and Windows OS integration are not included" describes the limits of the licensed Copilot, which concerns the sanctioned tool (P17) and not editor rules (P07).
units.anchor: Access is limited to the web browser only.

units.why: The Instructor Resources list an "Active Learning Strategies Catalog" and "Sample Prompts for Generating Active Learning Strategies", support for instructors to learn AI use (P63).
units.anchor: Sample Prompts for Generating Active Learning Strategies
units.policy: The university provides instructor resources: Evans Library's Ethical Use of Generative AI, an Active Learning Strategies Catalog, Sample Prompts for Generating Active Learning Strategies, and an AI-Era Framework.

documents.title: Student Academic Honesty Policy (Unauthorized Use of GenAI Tools section)
documents.stance_why: The excerpt says only that 'Unauthorized use of generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools in coursework constitutes a violation' and sends students to the Provost guideline and their instructors; what counts as authorized is set by the guideline and instructors, so the document delegates. Coder A said delegates and B said restrict; B's reading would make AI banned unless authorized, but this text does not state who authorizes or what is allowed.
documents.summary: Short paragraph in the honesty policy that classes unauthorized GenAI use in coursework as an honesty violation and points students to the Provost guideline and their instructors.

units.why: "Unauthorized use of generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools in coursework constitutes a violation" puts unauthorized AI use under the honesty policy, i.e. misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: Unauthorized use of generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools in coursework constitutes a violation
units.resolution_why: A must-not, B informs. This is the honesty policy's own statement that unauthorized GenAI use in coursework 'constitutes a violation', which forbids such use and is the main rule of the section, so must-not.

units.why: "must align with the university's commitment to academic integrity, ethical standards" restates the framework principle (P56), as in the guideline.
units.anchor: must align with the university’s commitment to academic integrity, ethical standards
units.frag_start: The use of GenAI within the University

units.why: Students are referred to the guideline and "must consult their instructors if they have any questions", telling unsure students to ask (P10).
units.anchor: must consult their instructors if they have any questions about the acceptable use
units.frag_start: Students are refered to the academic

notes: No school or computing policy found; course layer deferred. Only the 'Unauthorized Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Tools' paragraph of the honesty policy was coded. The guideline's reference list of AI tools and the Syllabus Template link were not coded. Document stance for the guideline is delegates (three sample options). Honesty-policy stance resolved to delegates (coders split delegates/restrict).
